{{nihongo|'''Takabe Shrine'''|高家神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Chiba)]].

'''Takabe Shrine''' (たかべじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Minamibōsō|ar|مينامبيوسو (تشيبا)|azb|می‌نامی‌بوسو، چیبا|ce|Минамибосо|ceb|Minamibōsō-shi|de|Minamibōsō|eo|Minamibōsō|es|Minamibōsō (Chiba)|fa|می‌نامی‌بوسو، چیبا|fi|Minami-Bōsō|fr|Minamibōsō|gl|Minamibōsō|id|Minamibōsō, Chiba|it|Minamiboso|ja|南房総市|ko|미나미보소시|mdf|Минамибоса|mzn|مینامی‌بوسو، چیبا|nl|Minamiboso|pl|Minamibōsō|pt|Minamiboso|ro|Minamibōsō|ru|Минамибосо|sv|Minamiboso|sw|Minamibōsō, Chiba|th|มินามิโบโซ|tl|Minamibōsō|tr|Minamibōsō|tt|Минамибосо|tum|Minamibōsō|uk|Мінамі-Босо|ur|مینامیبؤسؤ، چیبا|vi|Minamibōsō, Chiba|war|Minamibōsō, Chiba|zh|南房總市|zh_classical|南房總市|zh_min_nan|Minamibôsô-chhī|zh_yue|南房總|qid=Q873521}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|qid=Q80011}} (former {{ill|Chikura, Chiba|fa|چیکورا، چیبا|ja|千倉町|ko|지쿠라정|ur|چیکورا، چیبا|qid=Q5097510}}). It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is revered by people in culinary professions and soy sauce brewers as a shrine enshrining the “ancestral deity of {{ill|Cuisine|ar|مطبخ (أسلوب)|as|ৰন্ধনশৈলী|atj|Tcipakwan|ba|Аш-һыу (традициялар)|be|Кухня|bg|Кухня|bh|पकवान (इस्टाइल)|bn|রন্ধনশৈলী|br|Keginerezh|ca|Cuina|ckb|دەستاو|cs|Kuchyně (způsob přípravy jídla)|cv|Кухня (традици)|da|Kogekunst|el|Κουζίνα|eo|Kuirarto|es|Cocina (tradiciones)|eu|Sukaldaritza|fa|روش آشپزی|fi|Ruokakulttuuri|fr|Cuisine|gl|Arte culinaria|he|סגנון בישול|hi|पाकशैली|hr|Kulinarstvo|hy|Խոհանոց (ավանդույթներ)|id|Hidangan|ig|Cuisine|is|Matarhefð|it|Cucina (attività)|ja|料理|jv|Olahan|knc|Kәmbube|ko|요리|lad|Kuzina|lfn|Cosini|lt|Pasaulio virtuvės|mr|पाककला|ms|Masakan|nap|Cucina|new|नसापहः|nl|Keuken (kookwijze)|nn|Kokekunst|pa|ਪਕਵਾਨ|pcd|Tchuisinne|pt|Culinária|ro|Cuisine|ru|Кухня (традиции)|sc|Coghina|sh|Kulinarstvo|si|සූපවේදය|simple|Cuisine|sk|Kuchárske umenie|sq|Kuzhinieria|sr|Кулинарство|sv|Matkultur|sw|Kupika|th|การครัว|tr|Mutfak (kültür)|tt|Аш-су (традицияләр)|uk|Кухня|uz|Oshxona (anʼanalar)|vi|Ẩm thực|war|Panluto|zh|菜系|zh_min_nan|Liāu-lí|zh_yue|菜系|qid=Q1778821}}.”

===Enshrined deities===
It enshrines {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto}} (Takabe-no-Kami), and also {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu-Ōmikami}} and {{ill|Inari Ōkami|Q719665|qid=Q719665|lt=Inari Ōkami}}.

===History===
The origin of this shrine’s foundation is unknown, but the shrine’s history states that some descendants of the {{ill|Takahashi|ja|高橋氏|qid=Q11671376}}, descendants of Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto, may have moved to Awa Province, which was connected to their ancestral deity, and enshrined that deity as their ujigami. It is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} as “Takabe Shrine, {{ill|Asai District, Chiba|ja|朝夷郡|simple|Asai District, Chiba|qid=Q4803406}}, Awa Province,” but it appears to have later declined and disappeared, and its location remained unknown for a long time.

The origin of the current Takabe Shrine dates to the early {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}. In {{ill|Genna|de|Genna (Ära)|es|Genna|fa|گننا|fr|Ère Genna|id|Genna|it|Genna|ja|元和 (日本)|ko|겐나|ru|Гэнна|simple|Genna|sr|Гена|sv|Genna|tr|Genna|zh|元和 (日本)|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna}} 6 ({{ill|1620|Q6810|qid=Q6810}}), Takagi Kichiemon discovered a wooden statue and two mirrors beneath a cherry tree, and founded a shrine called “Shinmei-sha,” using them as sacred objects. About 200 years later, it was found that one mirror bore the inscription “Miketsu no Kami, Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto,” and it was judged to be the sacred object of the long-lost Takabe Shrine. In {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 2 ({{ill|1819|Q6967|qid=Q6967}}), a petition was submitted to the Yoshida office in Kyoto for official recognition, and the shrine was renamed from Shinmei-sha to Takabe Shrine.

A divided spirit of this shrine is enshrined at the {{ill|Higeta Shoyu|Q11329982|qid=Q11329982}} factory in {{ill|Chōshi|Q694317|qid=Q694317}} as a guardian deity of soy sauce brewing. It was enshrined there by Tanaka Naotarō (Kinchōshi), then president of the company and later author of ''Shōyu Enkakushi''. Through introductions by Tanaka Naotarō, Ishii Jibei (author of ''Nihon Ryōrihō Taizen''), and Miyake Koken of the Japanese Cuisine Research Society, the name of Takabe Shrine became known throughout Japan.
